significance: A marble temple about 24 km south-west of Nahan, begun in 1570 and dedicated in 1573 by the ruler of Sirmour using artisans brought from Jaipur, and later renovated by Maharaja Fateh Prakash in 1823 and Maharaja Raghubir Prakash in 1851. It is run by a temple trust headed by the Deputy Commissioner of Sirmaur and draws several million pilgrims a year.
story: A sacred stone is said to have appeared in a salt merchant's sack in 1570 after the goddess came to Ram Dass in a dream, and the temple was raised where she had shown herself.
